name: Music video
summary: A picture built to a song. The cut falls on the beat, the set is a stage, and the grade is loud. Story and place are cues that give way to a hook, a dance and a look.

philosophy.core_thesis: The song is the script, so images are cut to its beat and structure and a loud, memorable look sells the artist.
design_principles: Cut on the beat: at 120 bpm a beat lasts 0.5 s, so cut on every beat or every second beat, and change the shot on each chorus.
Build the clip in three layers: a performance, a story or a concept, and a graphic inset; keep each for 3 to 8 s.
Shoot the artist in a close-up for 30% or more of the runtime, with a lip-sync at 24 fps and the song at playback speed.
Use a strong key colour per section: one saturated hue at 40% or more of the frame, and swap it at the chorus.
Move the camera at the tempo: a push-in over 4 beats, a spin over 8 beats, a whip at the drop.
Use a wide lens of 14mm to 24mm for dance and a long lens of 85mm to 135mm for a face, with a shallow focus at f/1.8 to f/2.8.
Place one signature visual in the first 10 s and repeat it at the final chorus.
anti_patterns: A static, single, long take with no reference to the beat
A plain, unlit location with no concept
Dialogue and diegetic sound that mask the song
A scene that is cut for continuity and not for the music
A face that does not look into the lens
A look with no signature visual

composition.framing: A bold, wide-lens frame in 16:9 or 2.39:1, with the artist large and central, and a graphic shape or a colour wall behind.
composition.staging_in_depth: A stage of 3 planes: a foreground prop or a dancer, the artist in the middle and a coloured set or a screen behind.
composition.subject_placement: The artist on the centre or a third line; the dancers in a row or a ring about them, and the lens at a low or a Dutch angle.

principles.rule: Cut or move the camera on the beat and change the picture at each section of the song.
principles.value: 1 cut per 1 to 2 beats, 1.5 to 3 s average shot

principles.rule: Give each section one dominant saturated hue and swap it at the chorus.
principles.value: 1 hue at 40% or more, swapped at each chorus

principles.rule: Keep the artist's face or body as the brightest and largest mass of the frame.
principles.value: artist 40% to 80% of the frame height

principles.rule: Set a saturated coloured light against a dark ground for a hard, graphic image.
principles.value: key to fill 6:1, colour gels at full strength

principles.rule: Use a bilateral or a radial staging of dancers about the artist for the chorus.

camera_and_movement.movement: A push-in, a spin, a crane drop or a whip pan timed to the beat; the camera is a dancer of the piece.
camera_and_movement.support: Steadicam, jib, crane, dolly and a motion-control rig
camera_and_movement.camera_height: 0.3 to 2.5 m; low for a power shot and high for a choreography
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Push-in over 4 beats (about 2 s at 120 bpm); spin 180° to 360° over 8 beats; whip 180° per second

lens_and_format.aspect_ratio: 16:9 (1.78:1) or 2.39:1; 4:3 for the 1980s clips; 9:16 for a platform version
lens_and_format.frame_rate: 24 fps; 48 to 120 fps for slow motion; 30 fps for video
lens_and_format.shutter_angle: 180° (1/48 s); 90° for a strobed, sharp look
lens_and_format.focal_length: 14mm to 24mm (35mm format) for dance; 85mm to 135mm for a face
lens_and_format.aperture: f/1.8 to f/2.8 for a shallow face; f/5.6 for choreography
lens_and_format.focus: A shallow focus on the artist, with a rack to the dancers on the drop.

light.quality: Hard, coloured, theatrical light with a haze, beams, a strobe and a rim light on the artist.
light.direction: A back light and side light for a rim, a top light for a hero shot and a flat front light for a pop face.
light.key_to_fill_ratio: 6:1 for a dramatic clip; 2:1 for a pop clip
light.colour_temperature: A mix of 3200K and gels from 2000K to 9000K, with a coloured key
light.source: LED panels, gelled spots, a strobe and a haze machine

colour_and_grade.treatment: A loud, saturated, stylised grade that changes by section: one dominant hue, deep blacks and a clean rim light.
grade_recipe: Set the black point at 1% and keep the blacks deep and clean.
Push the saturation by +30% to +50% and shift the midtones to the section's hue by 10% to 20%.
Add a contrast curve of +30% with a hard shoulder at 92%.
Add a glow of 8% to 15% on the highlights and a chromatic split of 1 to 2 px at the edge.
Change the hue at each chorus, and keep one look for each section.
colour_and_grade.texture: Clean or stylised: either a smooth digital image or a deliberate grain of 10% to 20%

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 1.5 to 3 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 0.2 s for a flash cut to 15 s for a performance shot
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut to the beat and the lyric. Change the picture at each section of the song, and use a repeat or a loop at the chorus.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut on the beat, a flash frame, a whip, a match cut on a movement and a speed ramp.

sound.approach: The song is the only sound, in full range and at playback speed; effects are rare and added on the beat.
sound.dialogue: None, or a spoken intro of 5 to 15 s at the start of a clip.
sound.music: The full track, cut to a video version of 3 to 5 min, with an intro and an outro edit.
sound.loudness: −14 LUFS integrated, with a true peak of −1 dBTP for a platform release

titles_and_graphics.treatment: The artist and the song title in a lower third in the first 10 s; lyrics or graphics as a kinetic type on the beat.
titles_and_graphics.type: A bold display or a condensed sans-serif in a saturated colour, 2 to 5 s for the title card.

shot_primer.opening: Open on the signature image in the first 3 s, with the hook of the song already playing.

emotion.target_response: Excitement and desire: the viewer is carried by the beat and wants to see the artist again.

use_cases: short-form vertical clips on a track
video prompts for a dance or a performance
avoid_when: The brief needs a documentary tone or a quiet, long take.
The piece has no music track to cut to.

modifiers.how: Keep the colour and the beat; stage the artist on a central axis in a flat set, track at right angles and cut every 3 to 5 s.
Keep the song and the cut; shoot on a camcorder in 4:3, drop the gel light and let the focus hunt.

aspect_ratio.note: The 16:9 frame maps to 1.85:1; 4:3 is for the 1980s and 9:16 for a platform cut.

frame_rate.note: Slow motion runs at 48 to 120 fps.

colour_temperature.note: Gels from 2000K to 9000K colour the key.

sources.title: E. Ann Kaplan, Rocking Around the Clock: Music Television, Postmodernism, and Consumer Culture (Methuen, 1987)
Carol Vernallis, Experiencing Music Video: Aesthetics and Cultural Context (Columbia University Press, 2004)
Andrew Goodwin, Dancing in the Distraction Factory: Music Television and Popular Culture (University of Minnesota Press, 1992)
